target_customer: Tattoo artists and studios (current product); remote-first employers running recurring company meetings (original Venue.live product)
problem: Tattoo artists lose time to booking admin, chat and payment collection. The original product addressed dull recurring remote meetings such as all hands and town halls.
business_model: Booking fee on client payments (a third party reports about 10 percent, free for artists), unverified
product_category: Booking and payments software for tattoo artists; formerly remote meeting software

founders.name: Jason Goldlist
founders.background_notes: Also worked on operations for the Vancouver Olympic Games (YC page).

founders.name: Danilo Cabello
founders.background_notes: Computer engineer born in Brazil who moved to Canada in 2012, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video meeting layer built on WebRTC (founder skills listed) and later a booking and payments app are standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Meeting and booking software are copyable features; no moat is shown in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources opened; the company later moved to a tattoo booking product.

market_need_then: Accel describes remote-first employers struggling with engaging recurring meetings, and cites Shopify and PwC adoption and over 100K employees served in August 2022.

branding.domain_note: Moved from venue.live to venue.ink for the tattoo product; no purchase details found.

identity.visual_style: Not observed; the site fetch returned empty
identity.voice_and_tone: YC copy for the original product is playful (remote meetings more fun)

rebrands.why: Product shifted from remote meetings to tattoo booking; no source states the date or reason.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic real word shared with many venues; no press on the brand and a domain change tied to the pivot.

pivots.to: Venue.ink, booking app for tattoo artists
pivots.why: Not stated. Dated from the YC page founding year of 2023 and an App Store listing; the exact date is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Venue raised a 4M seed led by Accel in August 2022 for its remote meetings product, with Shopify and PwC as early users. The company later moved into a tattoo booking app and claims over 1,000 artists, a self-reported figure. No later rounds were found, so the story after the pivot is unclear.
notes: The YC page mixes Venue.live and Venue.ink content. The 4M figure appears in the TechCrunch headline cited on the YC page and in the Accel URL slug; the Accel article text does not state the amount. A newsletter reports the same round as 3.3M pounds. No competitors were named in the YC page or Accel post and no dated competitor source was found, so the list is empty. The site fetch for venue.ink returned empty.
